title: Conversation Handoff - Serialized Patch Spec (personal notes)
content:
Quick brain dump of an internal format for handing off an active conversation/session between runtimes or from client -> server (or client A -> client B via server). Goal: be compact, streamable, robust for partial delivery, and easy to apply as a series of deterministic patches so receivers can reconstruct equivalent inference context without heavyweight snapshots.

Summary and goals:
- Primary use case: mobile client upgrades / device switch / failover to dedicated runtime where we need to continue a multi-turn chat with minimal re-computation and without exposing raw logs.
- Format should support: incremental patching, sparse KV updates, token-range references into prior context, attachments (embeddings/recall bundles), and optional integrity/authentication metadata.
- Must be language-agnostic, friendly to streaming transports (HTTP/2, websockets, gRPC), and allow partial application if some patches are missing (graceful degrade).

Core principles:
1) Append-only patches: every handoff is a sequence of patches, each with an id and causal parent id(s).
2) Deterministic apply: given same base and same patch sequence, receiver arrives at identical context state.
3) Small by default: prefer token-index references to re-send full strings.
4) Privacy-first: support redaction markers and optional ephemeral-only fields.
5) Pluggable verification: signatures or MACs per-patch, optional per-field encryption.

High-level shape (informal):
- envelope (meta): {patch_id, parent_patch_id, session_id, seq_no, created_at, author, signature?} 
- body: list of ops where each op is one of: "insert_text", "delete_range", "upsert_kv", "evict_kv", "set_cursor", "attach_blob", "update_metadata".
- op metadata: each op carries a local_id, author, optional delta_cost_estimate, and optionally a hint (e.g., "this is prompt-system", "user-message").

Concrete example (textual JSON blob — treat as spec, not actual nested JSON field):
{
  "envelope": {
    "patch_id": "p-20250806-0007",
    "parent_patch_id": "p-20250806-0006",
    "session_id": "s-9fc3",
    "seq_no": 7,
    "created_at": "2025-08-06T15:42:21Z",
    "author": "client:device-3",
    "verification": "mac:v1:..."
  },
  "body": [
    {"op": "insert_text", "target": "turns", "index": 5, "value_ref": {"type": "token_range", "start": 120, "end": 158 } , "note": "user message continued"},
    {"op": "upsert_kv", "target": "kv-cache", "key": "chat:summary_v2", "value": "base64:eyJz...", "encoding": "json"},
    {"op": "attach_blob", "target": "attachments", "name": "user-image-ocr", "blob_ref": "blob-876", "mime": "application/json"} 
  ]
}

Notes on token_range value_ref: receivers are expected to have an indexed token store for the session. token_range references allow us to avoid re-sending large earlier messages. If receiver does not have the referenced token slice (cold start), it must request a fallback: either request the full text for that turn (via a patch requesting the string) or perform a server-side rehydrate operation.

Patch op catalogue (short):
- insert_text: insert a text fragment into a logical container (turns/messages). value can be inline string or value_ref.
- append_text: push to end of container. cheaper hint for streaming.
- delete_range: remove token range or turn index.
- upsert_kv: insert or replace a KV entry used for reused context (e.g., precomputed embedding). Value often stored as base64 compressed protobuf/json.
- evict_kv: remove a KV entry (privacy/cleanup).
- set_cursor: set active pointer (where next generation should continue).
- attach_blob: reference to a separate blob store; blob carries mime, length, content-hash, possibly encrypted key id.
- transform_instruction: a compact transformer for local-only transforms (e.g., normalize-whitespace, redact-emails) — optional and only executed if receiver approves trusted transforms.

Blob transport and streaming model:
- Small blobs (< 16KB): allowed inline as base64 in patch body.
- Large blobs: sent to blob-store URL returned by server during handshake; patch includes blob_ref metadata + chunk manifest (ordered chunk ids + checksums).
- Streaming: receiver can begin applying ops as they arrive; ordering guaranteed by seq_no. Patches carry an 'apply_hint' to indicate whether later patches may mutate earlier content (rare).

Integrity, privacy, and redaction:
- Each patch supports optional signature or MAC in envelope. For cross-device handoffs, server injects a server-signed attestation with allowed consumer roles.
- Redaction: ops can include redaction markers (redact_range) that indicate sensitive ranges that must be erased on apply. Redaction is authoritative: once applied, downstream receivers must expunge any persisted copy.

Compaction and snapshot strategy:
- After N patches or when payload grows > X bytes, produce a "snapshot" patch that contains a compact canonicalized representation of the session state (full text & kvs) and has parents set to all prior patches it subsumes. Receivers may drop prior patch history after snapshot verification. Snapshots help cold-starts and reduce replay.

Example ASCII diagram of flow (client A -> server -> client B):

client A (patch stream) -- chunked/http --> server ingestion queue -- assign seq_no --> storage + blob-store
      |
      | server returns ack with patch_id
      v
client B polls/longpoll/ws -> receives patch stream -> applies in order -> requests missing blobs by blob_ref if needed

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- How to minimize metadata bloat for long-lived chats (per-op author/ts adds up). Option: default to envelope-level author+ts and omit per-op unless explicit.
- How to handle branching: replay vs CRDT? For now prefer linear with explicit parents to keep deterministic apply; branching use-cases covered by separate sessions or explicit merged patches.
- Versioning: include spec_version in envelope; runtime must support at least two versions during rollout.
- Encryption: server-side KMS-wrapped content keys for blobs vs sender-side encryption. Tradeoff: sender-side gives better privacy but complicates key mgmt for cross-device pickup.

Local validation heuristics (receiver):
- reject patch if seq_no != expected and parent_patch_id not in local graph; request delta-repair API.
- verify content-hash for blobs; request retransfer on mismatch.
- if apply would cause context_size > configured_limit -> trigger compaction request or ask upstream to downgrade (trim oldest user turns).

Practical usage notes (personal):
- Keep first prototype minimal: support insert_text (inline), append_text, upsert_kv (inline small JSON), attach_blob (small inline), envelope with signature optional. No chunking in v0.
- Build server debug tooling that can rehydrate a session from patch sequence and export a flattened transcript. This will be invaluable for testing and repro.

Todos/TODO for follow-up:
- [ ] draft minimal v0 wire format (one-page) with examples for HTTP POST and websocket frame.
- [ ] prototype server-side rehydrate endpoint and a small CLI to apply patches to a local state store.
- [ ] write unit test vectors showing deterministic apply for concurrent patch arrival orders and for snapshot creation.
- [ ] sync with security on redaction guarantees and KMS approaches.

Notes-to-self: keep this doc as rapid notebook. If it stabilizes, move to proposals/ and create a PR with concrete schema definitions (use protobuf or compact CBOR).

End of scratchpad.
